substrate.profile: single ConfigMap co-locating semantic state, authority state, custody fence, and effect marker
substrate.linearization: API-server resourceVersion compare-and-swap on one object

positive_profile_checks: resourceVersion CAS on the same destination object

falsification_cases.name: stale owner after takeover
falsification_cases.expected: old owner/generation denied; new owner closes exactly one effect

falsification_cases.name: semantic state changes after native read
falsification_cases.expected: competing write changes resourceVersion; stale effect update conflicts; zero effect

falsification_cases.name: authority revoked after native read
falsification_cases.expected: competing write changes resourceVersion; stale effect update conflicts; zero effect

falsification_cases.name: exact valid fencing token replay
falsification_cases.expected: second effect denied; effect cardinality remains one

falsification_cases.name: split Lease fence and target object
falsification_cases.expected: COUNTEREXAMPLE: takeover of a separate Lease does not change target resourceVersion, so stale target mutation remains admissible

claim_boundary: This does not prove arbitrary Kubernetes mutations are natively fenced.
A separate Lease checked before a mutation is not enough; the proof deliberately demonstrates that gap.
The positive profile requires fence state and effect state to share the same Kubernetes object, or an equivalent server-side admission/transaction boundary.
No new governed-action semantic primitive is introduced.
The proof does not claim multi-object atomicity, cross-cluster transactions, or admission-webhook correctness.
